title: India opens 24,500 low-duty slots for UK-made cars in 2027
subtitle: Carmakers and their approved dealers can apply till 21 November for a share of the quota that cuts the steep Indian import tax on British cars.
content_html:
Picture a cricket stadium that keeps 24,500 cheap tickets for one big match. Once those tickets are gone, everyone else pays full price. That is close to how India will let in British cars in 2027. On 6 November 2026, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), the government office that runs India's import and export rules, opened applications for its 2027 quota of UK-made vehicles. The window is open from 6 November to 21 November 2026.

The quota covers 24,500 cars of different engine sizes and 2,750 transport vehicles. Cars inside the quota pay far less import tax than cars outside it. Under the deal, the tax on such cars falls to 10% from about 110%, step by step.

What is a quota, in plain words?

A quota is a fixed number. Here, it is the number of cars allowed in at a lower tax each year. Think of a samosa stall that sells the first 50 samosas at a discount every morning. Samosa number 50 gets the low price. Samosa number 51 pays the normal one.

The tax here is customs duty, a fee the government charges when goods enter the country. A simple example: if a car is worth Rs 10 lakh when it reaches an Indian port, a 110% duty adds Rs 11 lakh on top. A 10% duty adds only Rs 1 lakh. This sum only counts basic customs duty, to keep it simple.

The deal behind all this is the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, or CETA. The pact came into effect on 15 July 2026. According to Deccan Herald, it is the sixth free trade agreement put into force by the Narendra Modi government. The pact lets nearly 99% of Indian goods into the UK with zero duty.

This Mint video explains what gets cheaper now that the deal is live.

How the 24,500 cars are split

DGFT's Public Notice No. 39/2026-27, signed by Director General of Foreign Trade Lav Agarwal, splits the 2027 quota by engine size. Engine size is written in cc. A bigger number means a bigger engine.

  • 6,000 cars with engines up to 1,500 cc.
  • 6,000 cars with engines above 1,500 cc and up to 3,000 cc for petrol, or up to 2,500 cc for diesel.
  • 12,500 cars with bigger engines: above 3,000 cc for petrol or above 2,500 cc for diesel.
  • 2,750 goods vehicles, the kind that carry goods, other than electric or hydrogen ones.

All of them must come in as a Completely Built Unit. That means the whole vehicle arrives ready to drive, not as parts to be put together here.

About half of the car quota, 12,500 cars, goes to the biggest engines. Autocar Pro reported that the duty cut should especially help high-end British carmakers such as Jaguar Land Rover, Bentley, Aston Martin and Rolls-Royce.

Who can apply for these cheap tickets?

Not everyone. Only automakers, dealers and channel partners authorised by the makers of UK-built vehicles can apply. A channel partner is a firm the carmaker trusts to sell for it, like an official franchise.

The rules DGFT set in July, explained by Autocar Pro, add more checks:

  • Each applicant must show a pre-purchase agreement from the carmaker, saying how many vehicles it plans to bring in.
  • Every shipment needs a UK Certificate of Origin, a paper that proves the vehicle was made in Britain.
  • If firms ask for more cars than the quota allows, each gets a share in proportion to its request.
  • A firm that leaves a big part of its quota unused may get less the next year. Autocar Pro calls this a use-it-or-lose-it rule.
  • Permits stay valid for 12 months or until the end of the calendar year, whichever comes first.

Autocar Pro says these conditions keep unauthorised traders from using the low-duty quota on their own. So a trader cannot simply buy a few cars in London and bring them to Delhi at the low tax.

Why only 642 cars made it this year

The first round was tiny. For 2026, the government sought applications for around 5,000 vehicles, KNN India reported. Eight companies applied. In September, DGFT approved seven of these, covering 642 cars in all, an official told the news agency PTI.

That is far below the full first-year quota of 20,000 cars written into the deal. For calendar year 2027, the number of cars open for applications is 24,500.

Will British cars get cheaper?

The tax cut comes in steps. In the first year, duty on cars with engines above 3,000 cc (petrol) or 2,500 cc (diesel) drops to 30% from 110%, Outlook Business reported. For the smaller sizes, it drops to 50% from 66%. By the fifth year, the duty falls to 10%, and the yearly quota grows to 37,000 cars, according to Autocar Pro.

Over the first 15 years, India will let in 3.78 lakh petrol and diesel cars from the UK at the lower duty. Cars beyond each year's quota still pay the higher tax.

Will showroom prices fall? The rules only ask importers to "endeavour" to hand the saving to the final buyer, Autocar Pro reported. One market analyst told Autocar Pro that the quotas are small and the cuts are spread over time, so Indian carmakers are unlikely to be hurt.

In this Autocar India podcast, the team talks about why the deal matters for buyers of high-end cars.

What about electric cars and trucks?

Electric cars get a different deal. Battery, hybrid and hydrogen cars priced under GBP 40,000 (about Rs 44 lakh) get no duty cut at all, a move to shield Indian makers. Pricier ones get cuts only from the sixth year of the deal.

Trucks have their own track. Duty on UK-made trucks comes down to 8.8% from 44% within the quota by Year 5, and the truck quota rises from 2,500 in Year 1 to 3,500 from Year 5. The 2027 notice sets the goods vehicle quota at 2,750.

The deal runs both ways. From the sixth year, the UK lets in eligible Indian electric, hybrid and hydrogen cars with no duty within a yearly quota. Outlook Business named Tata Motors, Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki among the Indian makers set to gain.

What this means for you

For 2027, there are 24,500 low-duty car slots on offer, against the 642 cars cleared for the rest of 2026. For the firms that sell these cars, the deadline is 21 November 2026, and only sellers approved by UK carmakers can apply. For buyers, the tax drop comes in steps, and only cars inside the quota get the cut.
